toolkit_commands:
set -uo pipefail
rc=0

stage() { cp channel_drift.sh test_channel_drift.sh "$1/"; chmod +x "$1"/*.sh; }

# The suite colours its PASS/FAIL markers, so the raw line is
# "  <ESC>[32mPASS<ESC>[0m  <name>" and a literal grep for "PASS  x"
# never matches. Strip the escapes before any assertion reads them —
# NOT by loosening the greps, which would let "PASS" anywhere on the
# line satisfy a check meant to be about one named assertion.
plain() { sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$1"; }

# chan_mutation_check <label> <before-line> <after-line> <expected-red-test>...
chan_mutation_check() {
  local label="$1" before="$2" after="$3"; shift 3
  local mut; mut="$(mktemp -d)"; stage "$mut"

  # Rung 1: baseline.
  if ! (cd "$mut" && ./test_channel_drift.sh > base.txt 2>&1); then
    echo "::error::$label: the UNMUTATED suite already fails in the staging dir; this gate proves nothing"
    cat "$mut/base.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi
  # ...and a baseline with no assertions in it is not a baseline.
  local npass; npass="$(plain "$mut/base.txt" | grep -c 'PASS' || true)"
  if [ "${npass:-0}" -lt 10 ]; then
    echo "::error::$label: the baseline reports only ${npass:-0} passing assertions; the suite has been gutted"
    cat "$mut/base.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi

  # Rung 2: the assertions this mutation is supposed to trip must be
  # THERE, and green, before the mutation is applied.
  local t
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! plain "$mut/base.txt" | grep -qF "PASS  $t"; then
      echo "::error::$label: the baseline has no PASSING assertion named '$t' — it was renamed or deleted, and this guard is now blind"
      cat "$mut/base.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
    fi
  done

  # awk on an exact line, not sed: these anchors are full of
  # characters sed reads as syntax, and a mutation that silently does
  # nothing is the single failure mode this step exists to avoid.
  if ! grep -qxF "$before" "$mut/channel_drift.sh"; then
    echo "::error::$label: could not find the anchor line in channel_drift.sh; the code moved and this guard is now blind, fix it"
    rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi
  awk -v b="$before" -v a="$after" '$0 == b { print a; next } { print }' \
    "$mut/channel_drift.sh" > "$mut/m" && mv "$mut/m" "$mut/channel_drift.sh"
  chmod +x "$mut/channel_drift.sh"
  if ! bash -n "$mut/channel_drift.sh"; then
    echo "::error::$label: the mutant does not parse; it would fail for the wrong reason"
    rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi
  if cmp -s channel_drift.sh "$mut/channel_drift.sh"; then
    echo "::error::$label: the mutation changed nothing"
    rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi

  # Rung 3: the suite must fail, AND on the named assertions.
  if (cd "$mut" && ./test_channel_drift.sh > out.txt 2>&1); then
    echo "::error::$label: test_channel_drift.sh PASSED against the mutant"
    cat "$mut/out.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! plain "$mut/out.txt" | grep -qF "FAIL  $t"; then
      echo "::error::$label: the suite went red, but NOT on '$t' — the red is not attributable to this mutation"
      cat "$mut/out.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mut"
  echo "  ok  $label"
}

# 1. Regress into tool_drift.sh's path matching. This is the change
#    case_9c11948c originally proposed ("point tool_drift.sh compare at the
#    channel"), and it is wrong in both directions at once: it passes
#    a tampered file that kept its name, and it fails a compliant drop
#    the repo has since renamed. The whole reason this tool exists is
#    that it matches on content.
chan_mutation_check "match-on-path-not-content" \
  '    if [ -n "${BY_HASH[$hash]:-}" ]; then' \
  '    if [ -n "${BY_BASE[$(strip_prefix "$base")]:-}" ]; then' \
  'a renamed drop matching a blob at another path passes' \
  'a same-size, different-content drop fails' || rc=1

# 2. Drop the shebang test from the runnable classifier, keeping the
#    exec bit and the extension list. Reads as a simplification. It
#    means anything named like evidence is never checked, and
#    `bash TOG-nnn-findings.md` still runs it.
chan_mutation_check "shebang-test-removed" \
  "  case \"\$(head -c 2 \"\$f\" 2>/dev/null)\" in '#!') return 0 ;; esac" \
  '  :' \
  'a shebang alone makes a file runnable, whatever it is named' || rc=1

# 3. Honour an exemption that states no reason instead of refusing.
#    The tempting lenient default, and it turns the exemption file
#    into a mute button: one line, no explanation, detector silenced.
chan_mutation_check "unreasoned-exemption-honoured" \
  '        die "$exempt:$lineno: exemption for '"'"'$name'"'"' has no reason (want '"'"'<basename><TAB><reason>'"'"')"' \
  '        reason="(unspecified)"' \
  'an exemption with no reason is REFUSED, not honoured' || rc=1

# 4. Demote STALE to a warning, failing only on UNVERSIONED. Reads as
#    noise reduction. STALE is the case where a mirror STOPPED
#    mirroring — a file the operator installed from, edited in place
#    or swapped, and it is strictly more dangerous than one that was
#    never imported, because it looks reviewed.
chan_mutation_check "stale-demoted-to-warning" \
  '  if [ "$unver" -gt 0 ] || [ "$stale" -gt 0 ]; then' \
  '  if [ "$unver" -gt 0 ]; then' \
  'a same-size, different-content drop fails' || rc=1

# 5. Treat an ABSENT required mirror as nothing to report (case_2493ab4a).
#    The most tempting of the five: the suite right above it asserts
#    that "an exemption for an absent file is inert", so skipping a
#    file that is not there reads as the consistent behaviour. It is
#    the exact opposite for a required mirror — absence IS the
#    finding, and it is the state the channel is in until the
#    operator installs the README. This mutation makes the one thing
#    case_2493ab4a exists to detect report clean.
chan_mutation_check "absent-required-mirror-ignored" \
  '      missing=$((missing+1)); L_MISSING+=("$rbase  (want the bytes of $rpath)")' \
  '      :' \
  'a MISSING required mirror fails' \
  'the report names absence as its own category' || rc=1

# 6. Check a required mirror by PRESENCE rather than content. The
#    same defect as mutation 1, on the path where it matters most:
#    the README is the file whose entire content is the byte-for-byte
#    rule, so "a README is installed" is precisely the assurance that
#    is worth nothing. A truncated or hand-retyped copy passes.
chan_mutation_check "required-mirror-matched-on-presence" \
  '    if [ "$hash" = "${REQUIRED_HASH[$rbase]}" ]; then' \
  '    if [ -f "$rf" ]; then' \
  'a required mirror whose bytes are not the committed blob fails' \
  'a tampered required mirror is not reported as UNVERSIONED' || rc=1

# 7. Downgrade the missing-canonical-blob REFUSAL to a skip. case_70ae2474's
#    lesson, on this table: a comparison that did not happen must not
#    read as an answer. Renaming handoff-channel-README.md in the repo
#    without updating REQUIRED_MIRRORS would then silently stop
#    checking the README, and the run would go green having measured
#    nothing — the failure mode that is worse than a red.
chan_mutation_check "missing-canonical-blob-skipped-not-refused" \
  '      || die "required mirror source is not on $ref: $rpath (the table in $ME names a file this ref does not have; fix the table, do not delete the entry)"' \
  '      || continue' \
  'a ref with no canonical blob REFUSES rather than passing or failing' || rc=1

exit $rc

  chmod +x "$mut/channel_drift.sh"
  if ! bash -n "$mut/channel_drift.sh"; then
    echo "::error::$label: the mutant does not parse; it would fail for the wrong reason"
    rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi
  if cmp -s channel_drift.sh "$mut/channel_drift.sh"; then
    echo "::error::$label: the mutation changed nothing"
    rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi

  # Rung 3: the suite must fail, AND on the named assertions.
  if (cd "$mut" && ./test_channel_drift.sh > out.txt 2>&1); then
    echo "::error::$label: test_channel_drift.sh PASSED against the mutant"
    cat "$mut/out.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
  fi
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! plain "$mut/out.txt" | grep -qF "FAIL  $t"; then
      echo "::error::$label: the suite went red, but NOT on '$t' — the red is not attributable to this mutation"
      cat "$mut/out.txt"; rm -rf "$mut"; return 1
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mut"
  echo "  ok  $label"
}

# 1. Regress into tool_drift.sh's path matching. This is the change
#    case_9c11948c originally proposed ("point tool_drift.sh compare at the
#    channel"), and it is wrong in both directions at once: it passes
#    a tampered file that kept its name, and it fails a compliant drop
#    the repo has since renamed. The whole reason this tool exists is
#    that it matches on content.
chan_mutation_check "match-on-path-not-content" \
  '    if [ -n "${BY_HASH[$hash]:-}" ]; then' \
  '    if [ -n "${BY_BASE[$(strip_prefix "$base")]:-}" ]; then' \
  'a renamed drop matching a blob at another path passes' \
  'a same-size, different-content drop fails' || rc=1

# 2. Drop the shebang test from the runnable classifier, keeping the
#    exec bit and the extension list. Reads as a simplification. It
#    means anything named like evidence is never checked, and
#    `bash TOG-nnn-findings.md` still runs it.
chan_mutation_check "shebang-test-removed" \
  "  case \"\$(head -c 2 \"\$f\" 2>/dev/null)\" in '#!') return 0 ;; esac" \
  '  :' \
  'a shebang alone makes a file runnable, whatever it is named' || rc=1

# 3. Honour an exemption that states no reason instead of refusing.
#    The tempting lenient default, and it turns the exemption file
#    into a mute button: one line, no explanation, detector silenced.
chan_mutation_check "unreasoned-exemption-honoured" \
  '        die "$exempt:$lineno: exemption for '"'"'$name'"'"' has no reason (want '"'"'<basename><TAB><reason>'"'"')"' \
  '        reason="(unspecified)"' \
  'an exemption with no reason is REFUSED, not honoured' || rc=1

# 4. Demote STALE to a warning, failing only on UNVERSIONED. Reads as
#    noise reduction. STALE is the case where a mirror STOPPED
#    mirroring — a file the operator installed from, edited in place
#    or swapped, and it is strictly more dangerous than one that was
#    never imported, because it looks reviewed.
chan_mutation_check "stale-demoted-to-warning" \
  '  if [ "$unver" -gt 0 ] || [ "$stale" -gt 0 ]; then' \
  '  if [ "$unver" -gt 0 ]; then' \
  'a same-size, different-content drop fails' || rc=1

# 5. Treat an ABSENT required mirror as nothing to report (case_2493ab4a).
#    The most tempting of the five: the suite right above it asserts
#    that "an exemption for an absent file is inert", so skipping a
#    file that is not there reads as the consistent behaviour. It is
#    the exact opposite for a required mirror — absence IS the
#    finding, and it is the state the channel is in until the
#    operator installs the README. This mutation makes the one thing
#    case_2493ab4a exists to detect report clean.
chan_mutation_check "absent-required-mirror-ignored" \
  '      missing=$((missing+1)); L_MISSING+=("$rbase  (want the bytes of $rpath)")' \
  '      :' \
  'a MISSING required mirror fails' \
  'the report names absence as its own category' || rc=1

# 6. Check a required mirror by PRESENCE rather than content. The
#    same defect as mutation 1, on the path where it matters most:
#    the README is the file whose entire content is the byte-for-byte
#    rule, so "a README is installed" is precisely the assurance that
#    is worth nothing. A truncated or hand-retyped copy passes.
chan_mutation_check "required-mirror-matched-on-presence" \
  '    if [ "$hash" = "${REQUIRED_HASH[$rbase]}" ]; then' \
  '    if [ -f "$rf" ]; then' \
  'a required mirror whose bytes are not the committed blob fails' \
  'a tampered required mirror is not reported as UNVERSIONED' || rc=1

# 7. Downgrade the missing-canonical-blob REFUSAL to a skip. case_70ae2474's
#    lesson, on this table: a comparison that did not happen must not
#    read as an answer. Renaming handoff-channel-README.md in the repo
#    without updating REQUIRED_MIRRORS would then silently stop
#    checking the README, and the run would go green having measured
#    nothing — the failure mode that is worse than a red.
chan_mutation_check "missing-canonical-blob-skipped-not-refused" \
  '      || die "required mirror source is not on $ref: $rpath (the table in $ME names a file this ref does not have; fix the table, do not delete the entry)"' \
  '      || continue' \
  'a ref with no canonical blob REFUSES rather than passing or failing' || rc=1

exit $rc
